audit.whatIsWrong: Riposte is described everywhere as 'parries + stuns your combo', and the content layer tells you that throwing a Q-cone or an E into it means 'she'll Riposte it, stun you, and proc a Vital'. That is not what the ability does to those casts.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'This stab slows the first enemy champion hit, or stuns them if Fiora blocked an immobilizing effect with this ability.' Cunning Sweep is a damage cone and Lacerate is a slow — neither is an immobilise, so parrying them gets Ambessa slowed, not stunned. The only cast in her kit that arms the stun is Public Execution. That inverts the whole mind-game: the bait is cheap, and the ultimate is the one thing you must never lead with.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[1].d, dontsFull[0].d, report[5].t, whys[0], spikes[0].text and wants.foe[0] now state the immobilise condition.

audit.whatIsWrong: Riposte is referenced in eleven fields as the cooldown the lane runs on and its duration is never given once.
audit.why: Riposte is 24s at rank 1, dropping to 16s at rank 5 — the longest cooldown either champion has in this lane, and nearly two full Lacerate cycles for Ambessa. A player who knows it is 24 seconds baits it on purpose at level 2; a player told only 'track Riposte' waits for a number they never learn.
audit.corrected: tldr, winCon, phases[1].why, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[1].d and report[5].t now carry the 24s and 16s figures.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 2's 'why' claimed 'dash-resets stack your passive shield mid-trade', and Levels 4-5 was the generic 'lane-control window' template while the content layer calls that stage Fiora's.
audit.why: Drakehound's Step grants bonus attack range, damage, attack speed and an energy refund — no shield; Repudiation is Ambessa's only shield. At 4-5 her Q is 14-11s and E 13-10s against a 13-9.5s Lunge and an 11-9s Bladework, which is the real reason the stage belongs to Fiora.
audit.corrected: phases[1].why and phases[3].why now carry the real cooldowns and agree with the content layer.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was the generic 'the R lock isolates and finishes the chain — point it at the kill, not the tank', and Grand Challenge's cooldown is nowhere on the page.
audit.why: Grand Challenge is 110s at rank 1 against Public Execution's 130s, and it heals Fiora and her nearby allies if she lands all four Vitals or the target dies after even one. Ambessa's ultimate is both slower and the single cast that upgrades Riposte's stab into a stun, so the ordering of the two ultimates is the whole level-6 decision.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why and dontsFull[2].d now name Grand Challenge, its 110s cooldown and its heal condition.

audit.whatIsWrong: The itemisation line ends with 'his healing fights your pattern' — wrong pronoun, and it never says which abilities heal.
audit.why: Duelist's Dance restores health on every Vital she hits, and Grand Challenge heals her and her allies on a full four-Vital proc or a kill. Both are the reason Grievous Wounds has to land before her first item rather than after it.
audit.corrected: report[8].t now names Duelist's Dance and Grand Challenge and uses the right pronoun.

notes: Fiora is called 'he' in breakdown.feeding, breakdown.wave, report[9] and report[12], which are boilerplate duplicates I did not spend edits on. Ambessa's kit file flags grounding on Repudiation and grounding plus heal on Public Execution; Riot's descriptions of both abilities contain none of that, so I never told the player W denies Lunge. The content layer credits her R with 'passive armor-pen burst' and elsewhere with ability-hit healing; the armour-pen claim appears in most Ambessa matchups and the heal is only a derived flag with nothing in Riot's text behind it, so I left both alone rather than assert or delete them. Fiora's Riposte also disables, not only parries, for its brief duration — I kept the page's 'parries' wording since that is the half that matters for Ambessa's combo.
